title: API rate limit responses
text: An HTTP 429 response means the API is rate limiting the caller. Reduce concurrent requests, inspect any Retry-After header, and schedule retries with backoff and jitter. Record the request ID and timestamps. Before retrying a write, establish whether it is idempotent so a retry does not create a duplicate operation.

title: Expired access token
text: An API returning HTTP 401 may have an expired, missing or invalid access token. Check the authentication header and token expiration without copying token values into logs. Use the documented refresh or sign-in flow. A fresh valid token should be tried on the smallest reproducible request.

title: Authenticated request lacks permission
text: An HTTP 403 response can indicate that an authenticated identity lacks permission. Compare the account role, resource ownership and requested action against access policy. Record a redacted request example. Do not grant broad privileges just to make the error disappear.

title: SQLite database is locked
text: SQLite reports database is locked when another transaction prevents access. Look for long write transactions and unclosed connections. Keep transactions short, close connections reliably, and consider a bounded busy timeout. Capture transaction timing before changing journal settings or introducing retries.

title: Database connection pool exhaustion
text: When every database connection is in use, new requests can wait until they time out. Compare active connections, request concurrency and query duration. Look for connections that are never returned to the pool. Bound concurrency and fix connection leaks before simply increasing the pool size.

title: Background worker runs out of memory
text: A background worker killed for out-of-memory may be loading a dataset or too many batches at once. Inspect memory usage and termination logs. Reduce batch size, stream data where possible and limit concurrent workers. Checkpoint completed stages so an interrupted task can resume instead of repeating all work.

title: Duplicate delivery of background jobs
text: Message brokers may deliver a background job more than once. Give each logical operation a stable idempotency key, store completion state durably and make repeated delivery safe. Acknowledge only after required work is recorded. Test a crash between performing an operation and acknowledging its message.

title: Browser shows stale data
text: A browser may display an old response because a local or shared cache still holds it. Compare the network response with the rendered UI, inspect cache headers and cache keys, and check whether invalidation runs after a write. A forced refresh is a diagnostic, not a replacement for a correct invalidation strategy.

title: Cross-origin browser request blocked
text: A browser can block a cross-origin request when the server's CORS policy does not allow the page origin, method or headers. Inspect the preflight OPTIONS request and response headers in the network panel. Allow the intended origin explicitly; do not disable browser security or use permissive credentialed origins.

title: Handling a critical incident
text: When a critical production incident arrives, confirm impact, page the responsible on-call owner and preserve diagnostic evidence. Follow the incident process, communicate known facts and a next update time, and arrange coverage for lower-priority tickets. After recovery, document the cause, timeline and prevention work.
